public_rationale: Deep-food's repository history supports an earlier implementation of the same basic idea. It does not establish that Roose's coding models trained on it. Marcus presents that connection tentatively, and the available evidence neither verifies nor disproves it. The combined claim is therefore unresolved, with support for the predecessor-code component.
limitations: Similar functionality does not establish identical code or memorized generation.
Commit chronology is stronger evidence of code age than of first public availability.
Assessing only the firm predecessor statement would produce a narrower, more favorable conclusion.

our_interpretation: Existing code means an earlier implementation of the same basic photo-to-ingredients-to-recipes concept, not necessarily identical source code.
The target is the historical existence of such implementations before the post. No starting date is specified.
The training statement is explicitly tentative. Establishing that code existed does not establish that the particular models consumed it.
The combined proposition remains unresolved if the predecessor is established but the training inference cannot be checked.
criteria.support_condition: Dated records establish a qualifying predecessor before the post, and training records or a credible model-specific audit establish exposure to that implementation or comparable recipe-from-photo code.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records disprove the alleged predecessor or establish that the actual models did not train on the alleged class of code. Lack of disclosed training records alone is not contradiction.
